October 12, 2026

Homeland Security investigators raid Rep. Ilhan Omar's home

tags: politics, legal, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

Homeland Security Investigations, the criminal investigative arm within ICE, executed a search warrant at Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington, D.C. home on the morning of October 12, a move the Justice Department confirmed. Early reporting indicates the investigation concerns her immigration status and allegations that she filed false immigration paperwork, though no charges have been made public and no evidence of a crime has been presented. Omar said in a statement that she is safe and called the raid an attempt to target political enemies and weaponise federal law enforcement, adding that she will not be silenced. The raid comes roughly three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, inside the 60-day window in which Justice Department policy restricts overt investigative steps involving candidates and officials.

Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centres disrupt Russian bot networks

tags: war, tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Ukraine has struck three data centres belonging to Yandex, Russia's largest search and internet company, with drone attacks reported over the past several days. Cloudflare data cited in reporting shows bot traffic originating from that network falling to roughly 0.4 percent of the maximum number of HTTP requests recorded in the preceding two weeks. President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the strikes disrupted Russian bot activity and indicated further strikes on such targets will continue. The decline in automated accounts has been observed weeks before the United States midterm elections.

Pentagon raises Iran operations death toll to 21 service members

tags: war, defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon has revised its casualty count for operations against Iran to 21 U.S. service members killed and 865 wounded. The updated figure in the Pentagon's own database includes two additional non-combat deaths. In September, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had called reporting that the military's public death toll was incomplete a "complete LIE." The revision does not itself establish that the earlier figures were deliberately concealed.

American among 13 killed in strike on Riyadh airport as Trump weighs Houthi strikes

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual, @hunteralexanderhowell

Yemeni forces struck Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, killing 13 people, including an American, and wounding more than 300. A further strike on Sunday killed one person and injured 11, and the airport suspended operations. President Trump has said the United States may join Saudi strikes against the Houthis, but no decision has been announced.

Republican claim that Texas Senate nominee was in a mental facility collapses

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

MAGA influencer Nick Sorter circulated a recorded phone call claiming an Ohio facility, the Center of Hope, confirmed Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico had been discharged earlier in the week. The centre publicly denied Talarico had ever been a patient, and releasing such information would violate HIPAA. Talarico, who is diabetic and had been off the campaign trail with the flu, was documented attending a Kacey Musgraves concert in Texas on the night he was said to have been discharged. Figures including Trump, Stephen Miller and Ken Paxton amplified the claim, and a full six-minute version of the audio showed Talarico was never in the facility's system; an account alleging the circulating audio was AI-generated was reportedly suspended.

Federal judge halts tree removal in Washington and threatens contempt

tags: legal, politics, environment
sources: @aaronparnas

Judge Ana Reyes held an emergency hearing over the felling of hundreds of trees, many of them living and healthy, at the East Potomac Park golf course by the Trump administration without notification or permission. Reyes sharply criticised Justice Department lawyers in court, telling them that ignorance is not an excuse, and halted any further tree removal pending a later date. She warned that violating the order by two seconds would trigger contempt proceedings. Separately, a federal judge blocked the administration from airing taxpayer-funded advertisements, which were pulled overnight.

Musk spends $366 million to keep Republicans in control of Congress

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Elon Musk has put about $366 million into the 2026 midterm elections, including $276 million since July, making him the largest individual donor of the cycle according to campaign finance records. Of the third-quarter total, $158 million went to the Senate Leadership Fund, $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, $76 million to his own America PAC and $10 million to the Lone Star Liberty PAC backing Ken Paxton's Senate bid. House Democrats have said they want to investigate Musk's SpaceX government contracts and his role leading the Department of Government Efficiency. Musk spent about $290 million in the 2024 cycle, which included the presidential race.

FDA proposes expanding exemption allowing chemicals in food without safety review

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Food and Drug Administration is proposing to expand the threshold of regulation exemption, which currently allows certain compounds to be used in food contact materials such as packaging and processing equipment without safety review, provided they are not carcinogens and are present below 0.5 parts per billion. The proposed expansion, advanced under the Make America Healthy Again agenda, would allow such chemicals to be added directly to food as flavourings, preservatives, emulsifiers, processing aids, enzyme stabilisers and binders. Advocates say many of the compounds covered are considered dangerous even below the existing threshold and describe the change as a significant win for large food manufacturers.

Trump reported up to $273 million in securities transactions in August

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews

A financial disclosure shows President Trump reported 517 securities transactions in August worth between $74.3 million and $273.3 million. The largest purchase was between $5 million and $25 million in Meta stock on August 21, alongside $1 million to $5 million in SpaceX debt on August 18, two days before he signed a policy expanding commercial space transportation that could benefit SpaceX as a NASA and Pentagon contractor. Accounts also bought up to $50,000 in Tyson Foods shares the same day he signed a proclamation expanding low-tariff beef imports, with the order of events unclear. The White House said the president does not control the transactions, which are handled by independent managers and computer-based models; unlike recent presidents, his holdings are not in a blind trust.

Utah residents mobilise against Kevin O'Leary's Box Elder data centre

tags: tech, environment, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Kevin O'Leary's proposed Stratos data centre would take about 20,000 acres of Box Elder County and roughly 13,000 acre-feet of water a year, approved by MIDA, a state agency with an appointed rather than elected board, without an environmental study, public comment or a local vote. O'Leary accused Utah opponents of being paid foreign agents before admitting he had no evidence; Fox News apologised on air, NBC removed an interview, and he faces a defamation suit in Utah. Organisers are pressing for a statewide moratorium on data centres and have scheduled rallies at the Salt Lake City Capitol on October 20, 21 and 22, focusing on water transfers and air quality permitting as the main points of public input. Polling cited in the campaign indicates 75 percent of Americans would oppose an AI data centre being built near them.

Trump says Russia and Ukraine agreed to an energy ceasefire

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

President Trump announced on Sunday in a social media post that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire taking effect immediately, halting attacks on each other's energy infrastructure. He provided no details on the agreement's terms, duration or enforcement. Both countries have targeted energy facilities during the war, including oil refineries and power infrastructure, and fighting between the two forces has continued.

Hegseth military policy returns complaint handling to commanders

tags: defence, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has introduced a military policy described as "No More Walking on Eggshells," which places control over misconduct complaints back in the hands of unit commanders. The policy removes HR and civilian roles that handled anonymous complaints, requiring complaints to be made by an identified complainant, with commanders deciding whether a complaint is valid. Critics say the change will discourage women from joining or remaining in the military, and note that sexual assault in the ranks also affects men, with roughly one in six men experiencing some form of assault by adulthood.

Press bans and DOJ investigations draw comparisons to 1933 Germany

tags: politics, media, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

An analysis set out parallels between the Trump administration's actions in 2025 and 2026 and Germany between 1932 and 1933 ahead of the March 1933 legislative elections. It cited the barring of the Associated Press from the White House in February 2025, the subsequent banning of CNN, MSNOW and Politico by September 2026, and Justice Department investigations opened on October 10 into news organisations that stood in solidarity and refused to attend briefings. It also pointed to Executive Order 14399 asserting federal control over mail-in voting and the firing of Election Assistance Commission leaders, parts of which courts have blocked, National Guard deployments to cities over governors' objections with 2,500 troops still in Washington, D.C., some guarding ballot drop boxes, and calls for the indictment of Letitia James, James Comey and Adam Schiff.

Cyber attack defrosts refrigeration at French supermarket chains

tags: tech, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

A large-scale cyber attack targeted refrigeration systems at major French grocery chains, with hackers remotely triggering forced defrosting at numerous stores. French television reported more than 150 Intermarché shops and nearly 100 Coopérative U outlets were affected, and BFM TV reported that E.Leclerc, France's largest supermarket chain, was also targeted. Affected branches must discard fresh and frozen stock. The perpetrators and motive have not been established.

Israeli politician lays out case for annexing Gaza and the West Bank

tags: war, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

Israeli politician Moshe Feiglin argued in an interview that Gaza should be emptied and the West Bank annexed, describing Gaza itself rather than Hamas as the enemy. He said a child born in Gaza tomorrow would grow up to attack Israelis and that there is no possibility of changing or educating the population, citing the October 7 attacks as proof. The remarks were circulated as evidence of the political thinking behind Israel's conduct of the war.
